blocks.content: 1. INTRODUCTION TO PREPOSITIONS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Prepositions establish relationships between their objects (nouns/pronouns) and other words in a sentence.
Static state vs motion distinction is crucial: 'In' and 'On' denote position, while 'Into' and 'Onto' denote movement.
'Since' marks a specific point in time, whereas 'For' measures the duration/period of time.
'Beside' means adjacent or next to, while 'Besides' means in addition to.
Fixed prepositional usages after verbs, nouns, and adjectives form a major portion of error detection questions.

blocks.content:
A preposition is a word placed before a noun or pronoun to show its relationship with another word in a sentence.

It can indicate time, place, direction, cause, manner, possession, measure, and contrast.



Common prepositions include:

in, on, at, under, over, between, among, before, after, with, by, for, from, to, into, onto, across, through.



Prepositions are one of the MOST frequently tested topics in SSC examinations, especially in:

• Error Detection

• Cloze Tests

• Fill in the Blanks

• Sentence Improvement



Golden Principle:

Prepositions must be learned in context and combinations — not in isolation.
2. OBJECT OF A PREPOSITION (FOUNDATION RULE)

A preposition is ALWAYS followed by its object.



Structure:

Preposition + Noun / Pronoun / Gerund



Examples:

• She is fond of music.

• He is good at singing.

• They are interested in learning.



IMPORTANT RULE:

A verb cannot directly follow a preposition.



Incorrect: She is interested in learn.

Correct: She is interested in learning.
3. PREPOSITIONS OF TIME (VERY HIGH SSC WEIGHTAGE)

AT → Exact time / festivals / expressions

• at 5 PM

• at noon

• at night

• at Diwali



ON → Days and dates

• on Monday

• on 15 August

• on my birthday



IN → Months, years, centuries, long periods

• in July

• in 2025

• in the 18th century

• in the morning



IMPORTANT SSC TRAP:

• at night (NOT in night)
4. PREPOSITIONS OF PLACE

IN → Inside an enclosed space

• in the room

• in the box



ON → On a surface

• on the table

• on the wall



AT → Specific location or point

• at the gate

• at the station



SPECIAL RULE:

• in a car / taxi

• on a bus / train / plane / ship
5. PREPOSITIONS OF DIRECTION & MOVEMENT

TO → Movement toward a destination

• She went to Jaipur.



INTO → Movement from outside to inside

• He walked into the hall.



ONTO → Movement toward a surface

• The child climbed onto the bed.



FROM → Starting point

• She returned from Delhi.



OUT OF → Movement from inside to outside

• He ran out of the building.
6. IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE: IN vs INTO / ON vs ONTO

IN → Position

• The keys are in the bag.



INTO → Movement

• Put the keys into the bag.



ON → Position

• The book is on the table.



ONTO → Movement

• Place the book onto the table.
7. PREPOSITIONS OF CAUSE, REASON & PURPOSE

FOR → Purpose / benefit

• This gift is for you.



BECAUSE OF / DUE TO → Reason

• The match was cancelled due to rain.



FROM → Indicates suffering or cause

• He suffers from diabetes.
8. PREPOSITIONS AFTER VERBS (EXTREMELY IMPORTANT FOR SSC)

Always learn these as fixed combinations:



• depend on

• insist on

• believe in

• belong to

• suffer from

• apply for

• deal with

• approve of

• apologize for

• participate in

• recover from

• agree with (person)

• agree to (proposal)



SSC TRAPS:



Incorrect: discuss about the matter

Correct: discuss the matter



Incorrect: order for tea

Correct: order tea
9. PREPOSITIONS AFTER ADJECTIVES

• fond of

• afraid of

• proud of

• capable of

• aware of

• jealous of



• interested in

• weak in

• deficient in



• famous for

• responsible for

• eligible for



• similar to

• married to

• addicted to



MOST ASKED SSC RULE:

Different FROM (not than).
10. PREPOSITIONS AFTER NOUNS

• reason for

• demand for

• need for

• solution to

• increase in

• fall in

• attack on

• effect on

• influence on
11. BETWEEN vs AMONG

BETWEEN → Used for two persons/things.

• Divide the property between the brothers.



AMONG → Used for more than two.

• The teacher distributed chocolates among the children.



ADVANCED RULE:

Between can also be used for multiple entities when they are considered individually.
12. BY vs WITH

BY → Doer, method, proximity

• A novel written by Tagore.

• Travel by air.



WITH → Instrument, tool, companionship

• Cut with a knife.

• She came with her sister.
13. SINCE vs FOR

SINCE → Starting point

• since morning

• since 2019



FOR → Duration

• for two hours

• for many years
14. DURING vs WHILE vs FOR

rows: He is in the room (State) vs He walked into the room (Motion)
Sit beside me (Next to) vs Besides milk, buy bread (In addition to)
Since 1947 (Start point) vs For 5 years (Total period)
Killed by a hunter (Agent) vs Killed with a gun (Instrument)

blocks.content:
DURING → Followed by a noun

• during the match



WHILE → Followed by a clause

• while I was sleeping



FOR → Duration

• for three days
15. IN vs WITHIN

IN → Before the end of a time period

• I will finish it in an hour.



WITHIN → Inside a limit (not exceeding)

• Return the book within two days.
16. BESIDE vs BESIDES

BESIDE → Next to

• Sit beside me.



BESIDES → In addition to

• Besides English, she knows Spanish.
17. ABOVE vs OVER / BELOW vs UNDER

ABOVE → Higher level

OVER → Covering or vertically above



UNDER → Directly beneath

BELOW → Lower than a level
18. ACROSS vs THROUGH

ACROSS → From one side to another (surface)

• Walk across the bridge.



THROUGH → From inside something

• The train passed through the tunnel.
19. PREPOSITIONS WITH COMPARATIVES (SSC FAVORITE)

• senior to

• junior to

• superior to

• inferior to

• preferable to



Incorrect: superior than

Correct: superior to
20. DOUBLE PREPOSITION ERRORS

Do NOT use unnecessary prepositions.



Incorrect: return back

Correct: return



Incorrect: repeat again

Correct: repeat

items: Avoid redundant prepositions: Words like 'discuss', 'order', and 'comprise' do not take prepositions when used in the active voice (e.g., avoid 'discuss about').
Distinguish Agent vs Instrument: Use 'By' for the person/agent doing the action and 'With' for the tool/instrument used.
Use 'Between' when referring to two distinct items/persons, and 'Among' for more than two.
Watch out for double preposition errors in comparative degree structures and prepositional phrases.

blocks.content: 21. HIGH-PROBABILITY SSC RULES

1. Always use a gerund after a preposition.

2. Learn verb-preposition pairs.

3. Avoid extra prepositions.

4. Focus on context, not translation.

5. Remember fixed expressions.

6. Practice confusing pairs regularly.
22. COMMON ERRORS IN EXAMINATIONS

Incorrect: She is married with a doctor.

Correct: She is married to a doctor.



Incorrect: He is good in English.

Correct: He is good at English.



Incorrect: He insisted to go.

Correct: He insisted on going.
23. PRACTICE QUESTIONS (SSC LEVEL)

Fill in the blanks:



1. She is fond ___ dancing.

2. He insisted ___ paying the bill.

3. Divide the sweets ___ the two boys.

4. The river flows ___ the bridge.

5. He apologized ___ his mistake.



Error Detection:



1. He is superior than me.

2. She discussed about the problem.

3. The train will arrive in Monday.



Answers:

of, on, between, under, for



Errors:

than → to

remove about

in → on
24. CHAPTER SUMMARY

Prepositions are essential for forming grammatically correct sentences.



Key Takeaways:



• Always attach an object after a preposition.

• Use gerunds after prepositions.

• Memorize fixed combinations.

• Master confusing pairs.

• Avoid redundant prepositions.
